pure-announcement.rationale: This is a practitioner's own reasoning about a technique, not a product launch or release note.

duplicate.rationale: reachability-based-dead-code-detection covers only the static reachability-graph technique and its entry-point failure mode; it says nothing about confirming a static finding against runtime execution evidence before deleting, which is this note's core point.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The reasoning is checkable against the named static tools (debride, unused) and dynamic tools (coverband, scythe) and is a verifiable technical argument, not an unsourced claim.

durability.rationale: The trade-off itself - static analysis is cheap and fast but imprecise, dynamic analysis is accurate but costly and only as good as its observation window - is a methodological point about program analysis independent of which specific tools (debride, coverband, scythe) implement it, so it will outlast any one tool.

actionability.rationale: It gives a concrete decision rule for the moment of deleting flagged code: do not trust a static-only finding, and do not trust a dynamic-only absence-of-execution reading until it has run long enough to rule out rarely-used-but-live paths.

atomicity.rationale: One idea - static flags cheaply but imprecisely, dynamic confirms accurately but needs sufficient observation time, so deletion confidence requires both - is stated independently of the specific Ruby tools used to illustrate it.
